claims.claim: Vancouver council authorized a People's Audit of 2026 budget cuts covering $120 million, with a public staff report due in the first quarter of 2027, and only Mike Klassen voted against it.
claims.episode_span: COPE Councillor Sean Orr's audit requires staff to report in public in the first quarter of 2027 on the effects of $120 million in cuts
claims.source_title: Vancouver City Council authorizes audit into 2026 budget cuts
claims.supporting_quote: The new council's "People's Audit,” proposed by COPE Coun. Sean Orr, mandates that city staff report publicly in the first quarter of 2027 on the specific impacts of these $120 million in cuts.

claims.claim: Council directed staff to implement a June report on eliminating traffic injuries, including 30 or 40 km/h speed-limit recommendations, after three pedestrians were killed and two injured since late October.
claims.episode_span: including recommendations for 30 or 40 km/h limits on major streets, after three pedestrians were killed and two injured since late October
claims.source_title: Vancouver City Council authorizes audit into 2026 budget cuts
claims.supporting_quote: In their place, the council directed staff to implement a June report on eliminating traffic-related injuries, including recommendations for 30 or 40-kilometre-per-hour speed limits on major streets.

claims.claim: Council delayed the gas water-heater ban until January 1, 2028, and rescinded the robot food-delivery pilot.
claims.episode_span: It put off a gas water-heater ban until January 1, 2028
claims.source_title: Vancouver City Council authorizes audit into 2026 budget cuts
claims.supporting_quote: The council delayed the implementation of the gas water heater ban until January 1, 2028, and asked staff to work with residents and developers to ease the permitting process for electric homes and utilities.

claims.claim: Lorne Doerkson is to be sworn in Friday at Government House as B.C.'s 38th premier and unveil his cabinet, forming the first Conservative government in almost a century.
claims.episode_span: Lorne Doerkson is to be sworn in today at Government House as British Columbia's 38th premier
claims.source_title: British Columbia’s premier-designate Lorne Doerkson, cabinet to be sworn in
claims.supporting_quote: British Columbia’s first Conservative government in almost a century will take the reins of power when Lorne Doerkson becomes premier and unveils his first cabinet.

claims.claim: Elections BC's official count is 64 Conservatives, 27 NDP members and two Greens, with judicial recounts in two ridings decided by fewer than 50 votes.
claims.episode_span: Elections BC's official count is 64 Conservatives, 27 NDP members and two Greens
claims.source_title: British Columbia’s premier-designate Lorne Doerkson, cabinet to be sworn in
claims.supporting_quote: Elections BC says the official seat count is 64 Conservatives, 27 NDP members and two Greens, although there will be a judicial recounts for two ridings won each by a Conservative and a New Democrat by fewer than 50 votes.

claims.claim: Stewart Prest expects a relatively smaller cabinet than under John Horgan and David Eby.
claims.episode_span: Stewart Prest expects a relatively smaller cabinet than under John Horgan and David Eby
claims.source_title: British Columbia’s premier-designate Lorne Doerkson, cabinet to be sworn in
claims.supporting_quote: UBC political science lecturer Stewart Prest says he expects a “relatively smaller cabinet” when compared with to the NDP cabinets under late premier John Horgan and departing Premier David Eby.

claims.claim: The Surrey Police Service will take over full policing duties on March 31, 2027, with RCMP support as required until the end of March.
claims.episode_span: the Surrey Police Service will take over full policing duties for the city on March 31, 2027
claims.source_title: Surrey police aim to complete transition in March, but cost and staffing questions remain
claims.supporting_quote: Under a plan revealed this week, the Surrey Police Service will take over full policing duties for the city on March 31, 2027.

claims.claim: Parks Canada and the Canadian Armed Forces no longer plan to end Operation Palaci, the avalanche-control program in Rogers Pass.
claims.episode_span: they no longer plan to end Operation Palaci
claims.source_title: Canadian military will keep firing howitzers to trigger B.C. avalanches, pausing plan to end program
claims.supporting_quote: Parks Canada and the Canadian Armed Forces say that after "further consideration," they no longer have plans to end Operation Palaci, a long-running avalanche control program in Rogers Pass through the Selkirk Mountains in Glacier National Park.

claims.claim: A B.C. Supreme Court judge ordered the substantially started label for the KSM Mine sent back for deep consultation with a First Nation.
claims.episode_span: a decision labelling the KSM Mine in northwestern B.C. "substantially started" be sent back to the provincial government
claims.source_title: Court orders 'deep consultation' between B.C. gov't, First Nation over KSM Mine environmental approval
claims.supporting_quote: A B.C. Supreme Court judge has ordered that a decision to label a mine in northwestern B.C. as "substantially started" be sent back to the provincial government, and that it must have "deep consultation" with a First Nation with territory in the area.

claims.claim: Dexterra lost the SkyTrain cleaning contract, and the union for about 160 janitors accuses the employer of union-busting.
claims.episode_span: Dexterra has lost the SkyTrain cleaning contract, and the union for about 160 janitors
claims.source_title: Dexterra Loses SkyTrain Cleaning Contract
claims.supporting_quote: The union for about 160 SkyTrain janitors has accused the employer of union-busting and a toxic work environment.

claims.claim: Landlords fined $90,000 for subdividing an East Vancouver home into 21 sleeping rooms are now facing prosecution over a West Side property.
claims.episode_span: Landlords already fined $90,000 by the Residential Tenancy Branch
claims.source_title: Vancouver landlords fined $90K now facing prosecution over West Side property
claims.supporting_quote: B.C.'s Residential Tenancy Branch recently fined the landlords $90,000 for subdividing an East Vancouver home into 21 sleeping rooms, with at least 17 tenants.

claims.claim: Kimberly Polman wrote that travelling to Syria to marry an ISIS supporter was a mistake, in a letter filed for a Vancouver sentencing.
claims.episode_span: Kimberly Polman, who travelled to Syria to marry an ISIS supporter, wrote that she realizes it was a mistake
claims.source_title: B.C. woman who travelled to Syria to marry ISIS supporter says she realizes it was a mistake
claims.supporting_quote: That admission was in a letter Kimberly Polman wrote that's part of the agreed statement of facts filed in her case that a Vancouver judge will consider in her upcoming sentencing.

claims.claim: VPD Chief Steve Rai said he told Mayor Pete Fry the department wants to work with him and be responsible while seeking a 2027 budget hike.
claims.episode_span: Chief Steve Rai said he told Mayor Pete Fry the department wants to work with him and be responsible
claims.source_title: Vancouver Police Department seeks 2027 budget hike at first post-election board meeting
claims.supporting_quote: 'I told Mayor Pete Fry: 'We want to work with you.' We want to be responsible. But at the same time, I have a responsibility on public safety' — VPD Police Chief Steve Rai

claims.claim: The Seattle Kraken defeated the Vancouver Canucks 5-1, with Berkly Catton scoring his first NHL hat trick.
claims.episode_span: Berkly Catton's first NHL hat trick carried the Seattle Kraken past the Vancouver Canucks 5-1
claims.source_title: Catton gets first NHL hat trick, Kraken ease past Canucks
claims.supporting_quote: Berkly Catton scored his first NHL hat trick for the Seattle Kraken, who defeated the Vancouver Canucks 5-1 at Climate Pledge Arena on Thursday.

claims.claim: Leevi Merilainen made 38 saves and the Kraken set a franchise record with 24 shots in the first period.
claims.episode_span: Leevi Merilainen made 38 saves, matching his career best, while Seattle put 24 shots on net in the first period
claims.source_title: Catton gets first NHL hat trick, Kraken ease past Canucks
claims.supporting_quote: The Kraken outshot the Canucks 24-5 in the first period, which set a new Seattle franchise record for shots in one period.

claims.claim: Brendan Gallagher left the Kraken game with a lower-body injury, and Filip Hronek played 30:11.
claims.episode_span: Brendan Gallagher left with a lower-body injury. Filip Hronek played 30 minutes and 11 seconds
claims.source_title: I Watched This Game: The Canucks are running Filip Hronek into the ground
claims.supporting_quote: Add in nearly four minutes on the penalty kill and over three minutes on the power play, and Hronek finished the night with 30:11 in ice time, leading all players on Thursday night by a wide margin.

claims.claim: Whitecaps FC host Real Salt Lake in a best-of-three series opening Sunday, November 22, at 6:30 p.m. at BC Place, after Real Salt Lake beat Seattle on penalties.
claims.episode_span: Game 1 is Sunday, November 22, at 6:30 p.m. at BC Place
claims.source_title: Whitecaps FC to face Real Salt Lake in Round One Best-Of-3 Series
claims.supporting_quote: Game 1 will take place this coming Sunday, November 22 at 6:30 p.m. PCT at BC Place.

claims.claim: Olivia Rodrigo plays Rogers Arena on December 1 and 2 at 7 p.m., both shows sold out, with Devon Again supporting.

claims.supporting_quote: The shows are on Dec. 1 and 2.
